strengths: The Global Workspace Layer offers a plausible architectural contribution by combining low-dimensional memory, sparse token selection across a batch, and associative retrieval in a modular addition to ViT. :codex-file-citation{path="/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b03/review-experiment-cu8t8ff5/call-a1c157b171194361b4cec36abd2ac932/manuscript.pdf" purpose="source"}

The comparisons against ViT show consistent benefits. AiT-Medium uses 45.9M parameters versus ViT-Base's 85.7M, while improving CIFAR-100 accuracy from 57.92% to 60.58% and ImageNet100 accuracy from 34.62% to 36.72% (Tables 1–2). These results support improved parameter efficiency within the evaluated configurations.

The relational reasoning gains are substantial: AiT-Small achieves 76.82% on Sort-of-CLEVR relational questions versus 51.75% for ViT-Small and 73.43% for Coordination (Table 6). This extends the empirical contribution beyond image classification.

The component ablations are useful and report variability across runs. Removing the bottleneck reduces CIFAR-10 accuracy from 83.34% to 75.40%, while removing the balance loss or replacing Hopfield retrieval produces smaller declines (Table 3). The supplementary visualizations also provide evidence of increasingly diverse token selection.
weaknesses: The proposed balance loss has a substantive mathematical problem. In Equations 3–4, A is defined through softmax, so every entry is positive and the selected-instance count is identically M, making its variance zero. If A instead denotes masked top-k attention, the indicator count is nondifferentiable and supplies no useful gradient without an estimator that is not specified. Thus, the claimed two-component training objective is not established as written, although the importance component could still explain the ablation gains.

The memory protocol is insufficiently specified for reproducibility and interpretation. Section 3.2 says explicit memory is frozen during evaluation, whereas Appendix F reports benefits from retaining the memory-writing cross-attention at test time. The manuscript does not distinguish persistent updates from temporary batch-conditioned memory. Because tokens from different images are pooled, this distinction determines whether predictions depend on other test images or evaluation order. The interaction between gradient learning and EWMA updates is also unclear.

The associative-retrieval claims exceed the technical support. Equation 6 specifies an argmin, but the implementation uses one update; energy reduction does not establish convergence to a minimum or a stored prior. Moreover, the standard one-step modern Hopfield update is equivalent to softmax attention with tied keys and values. The W/O Hopfield ablation substitutes a differently parameterized multi-head attention module, so it does not isolate the benefit of the claimed energy-based mechanism from parameterization and regularization effects.

The broad sparse-efficiency claims need qualification. AiT retains dense self-attention, and memory writing computes attention scores before top-k selection. Table 1 supports savings relative to deeper ViTs, but AiT-Small uses 15.8M parameters versus Coordination's 2.2M. The single-block study provides useful narrower evidence; without runtime, peak-memory, or sequence-length scaling measurements, general computational-efficiency claims remain insufficiently supported.

Practical competitiveness is weakly established. ImageNet100 is compared only against ViT, and the relational evaluation omits the relation-network method from the cited benchmark paper [14]. The reported 36.72% ImageNet100 and 30.05% Oxford Pet accuracies make comparisons under stronger training recipes particularly relevant. Benchmark leadership is unnecessary, but these experiments leave uncertainty about the usefulness of the gains beyond the supplied setups.

There are additional, correctable reporting issues: Section 4.1 gives an initial learning rate of 1e-5 while Table 8 gives 1e-4, and the ImageNet100 class subset is unspecified. These are secondary concerns. My Weak Reject recommendation is driven principally by the unresolved objective and memory semantics, together with inadequate isolation of the central retrieval claim, despite the worthwhile empirical improvements.
